To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the New York Freedom of Information Law, I hereby request the following records:

November 5, 2026
Dear FOIL Officer:
Please e-mail to the undersigned, or, if necessary, send copies of all records and documents and materials relating to the matters listed below concerning Judge Kathleen Waterman Marshall ("Subject") that were sent to the administrative justices (or their chambers), including but not limited to:

 	Suzzane J. Adams
 	Norman St. George   
        Deborah A. Kaplan   
         Adam Silvera
 	Jeffrey S. Sunshine
 	Joseph Zayas

This FOIL request covers the period January l, 2019, through the date of your response. My requests are as follows:

1.      All data, records or information of any kind relating to complaints submitted by petitioners, respondents, attorney's or other representatives or advocates, or any others against the Subject;
2.	Total number of complaints submitted by petitioners, respondents, attorneys or other representatives or advocates, or any others, against the Subject;
3.	All data, records or information of any kind relating to internal or external investigations into the Subject; and
4.	All data, records or information of any kind relating to disciplinary actions against the Subject.

If all the requested records cannot be emailed to me, please inform me by email of the portions that can be emailed and advise me of the cost for reproducing the remainder of the records requested ($0.25 per page or actual cost of reproduction).

If the requested records cannot be emailed to me due to the volume of records identified in response to my request, please advise me of the actual cost of copying all records onto a CD.

If this request is too broad or does not reasonably describe the records, please contact me via email, so that I may clarify my request.

If for any reason any portion of my request is denied, please inform me of the reasons for the denial in writing and provide the name, address and email address of the person or body to whom an appeal should be directed.

As you know, the Freedom of Information Law requires that an agency respond to a request within five business days of receipt of a request. Please note that if the requested records cannot be provided within twenty business days, Article 6 of the Public Officers Law mandates that the agency state in writing both the reason för the inability to grant the request within twenty business days and a date certain within a reasonable period, depending on the circumstances, when the request will be granted in whole or in part.

I trust that the Office of Court Administration will comply with these laws.

Thank you.
 
Joseph G. Brosnan

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Joseph Brosnan

title: FBI: Dancer Anna Halprin and the Tamalpa Institute

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: FBI: Dancer Anna Halprin and the Tamalpa Institute
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Under the Freedom of Information Act, 5 U.S.C. § 552, I request access to and copies of all records maintained by the Federal Bureau of Investigation concerning choreographer and dancer Anna Halprin (born Anna Schuman, July 13, 1920; died May 24, 2021) and the Tamalpa Institute (founded 1978 in Marin County, California).

Proof of death:

Ms. Halprin died on May 24, 2021, at age 100. NPR’s obituary is available at https://www.npr.org/2021/05/25/1000217732/remembering-anna-halprin-a-pioneering-choreographer. I ask that the FBI treat this as proof of death and process the request without requiring a privacy waiver from the subject. I recognize that privacy interests of living third parties named in responsive records may still be asserted.

Background: 

Halprin founded the San Francisco Dancers’ Workshop in 1955. Her students and collaborators included Simone Forti, Yvonne Rainer, Trisha Brown, Meredith Monk, John Cage, Terry Riley, La Monte Young, and Morton Subotnick. Her 1965 work Parades and Changes was banned after its 1967 premiere at Hunter College in New York, and arrest warrants were issued for the performers. In the late 1960s she staged Ceremony of Us with Black and white dancers, and her later work included the community performance Planetary Dance. Given her profile and the period’s interest in avant-garde and countercultural activity, responsive records may exist.

Scope:

Please search the Central Records System, including main files and cross-references, electronic surveillance indices, and the records of FBI Headquarters and the San Francisco and New York Field Offices, for records mentioning or referencing:

1. Anna Halprin, including the variants Ann Halprin, Anna Schuman, Anna Schuman Halprin, Anna S. Halprin, and Mrs. Lawrence Halprin.

2. The Tamalpa Institute and the San Francisco Dancers’ Workshop (also Dancers’ Workshop of San Francisco and Dancers’ Workshop Company).

3. Any investigation, inquiry, surveillance, informant reporting, or intelligence communication concerning her performances, workshops, or community art events, including the 1967 Hunter College performance of Parades and Changes and the related arrest warrants.

The date range is 1945 through the present. If any responsive records have been transferred to the National Archives and Records Administration, please identify them and their location. Please specifically search official correspondence either to or from director J. Edgar Hoover that references Halprin, her work, or the Tamalpa Institute. 

Determination and exemptions. I look forward to a determination within the statutory 20 working days. If any material is withheld or redacted, please cite the specific exemption for each redaction, release all reasonably segregable portions, and provide an index of withheld material sufficient to assess each claimed exemption.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robert Delaware
